one_line_pitch_to_sam: It's a grey test map where the sword looks sick and you can dance off a tower, but there's no actual game and nothing keeps score.

moments.why: Only survives as 'you spawn and it's just a grey floor'; nothing happened there.
Running around was fine and felt like nothing.
Bunny-hopping between things left no trace.
Five seconds of 'we're ninjas' with nothing to sneak up on; gone by morning.
The truss is only remembered as the tower you dance off; the made-up race and the empty top are forgotten.
Dancing off the edge with flailing arms was the biggest shared laugh, though it wore out after a few repeats.
Remembered as a random pool with nothing at the bottom; 'mid, it's just water'.
Sitting on the bench and getting killed on it felt like nothing even at the time.
Shadow-boxing the air only fed the general 'game is on mute' impression.
First silent punch on the dummy was overwritten by the sword.
The combo was a small spark that nothing built on.
Finding the kick was pleasant for a second and never mattered again.
Learning the block key is forgotten; only what blocking did to the fight stuck.
'You have a sword' is how they describe the game, but the equip moment itself is not retold.
Both agree the slash looks sick; it's the one thing they praise about the game.
The dummy lying down then reappearing and giving nothing became the 'immortal guy' joke and a complaint.
Hitting a friend working is the premise of the retelling, but the mushy trading itself blurred together.
The bet fight where the loser had to say the other is better, plus the disputed 7-2 score, is the headline story.
Blocking looked like lag with no feedback and killed the fight; Kai is still annoyed.
Waving hello and goodbye was sweet but too small to survive.
'Dancing to nothing' is remembered only as the setup for the jump; the failed synced dance party is forgotten.
The silent laugh over Kai's body was cursed and became the running gag.
Guessed emotes being swallowed was a string of small letdowns, not a story.
Dance cancelling on movement was a minor annoyance that didn't stick.
The dummy 'just stands there staring at you' gets one line as part of the immortal-guy bit.
The absurdly long run to the edge of the world is remembered for the commitment, not the destination.
No rounds, leaderboard, ranks or shop is the reason they give for not playing again.
